title: A spacing scale with calc()
summary: One --space unit multiplied with calc() sets every gap and padding, so changing one number rescales the page.
explanation: --space: 4px is the base unit. Every spacing value is a multiple of it: calc(var(--space) * 4) is 16px. Consistent multiples are what make a layout feel tidy, and naming them stops random numbers like 13px creeping in.
Because the unit is a variable, a compact section only needs to redefine it. .compact sets --space: 2px, and everything inside shrinks to half: padding, gaps and margins together.
calc() needs spaces around + and - (calc(1px + 2px)); for * and / they are optional but help reading.
tryThis: Change --space in .page to 6px: the whole page breathes more.
Remove the compact class from the second card in Items.
Write padding: calc(var(--space) * 2) calc(var(--space) * 6) on .tag: a wide, short pill.
